chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hurayz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

On the Day of Resurrection, God the Exalted will present a proof against five groups: the child, the one who died between the Prophets, the one who lived at the time of the Prophet but did not have intellect (to understand), the simple-minded (ablaha), the insane one who does not understand, the deaf, and the mute. Each of them will present a proof to God the Exalted. He said: God will send a messenger to them, and a fire will be kindled for them, and he will say to them: Your Lord commands you to jump into it. Whoever jumps into it, it will be cool and safe for him, and whoever disobeys will be driven to the Fire.

The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: Some people of Kalam (theology/discourse) deny this, saying: It is not permissible that there be obligation/trial in the Abode of Recompense. The Abode of Recompense for the believers is Paradise, and the Abode of Recompense for the disbelievers is Hell. This obligation/trial is from God the Exalted for them in addition to Paradise and Hell, so their being charged is not in the Abode of Recompense itself, but then He returns them to the Abode they deserve by their obedience or disobedience. Therefore, there is no basis for denying this. And there is no power except with God.

key_terms.الْأَبْلَهَ: The simple-minded (one with basic intellect but limited understanding)
key_terms.بَيْنَ النَّبِيِّينَ: Between the Prophets (period of inter-prophetic gap)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five groups tested on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this narration to address the theological debate regarding *taklif* (obligation) in the afterlife, specifically refuting the *Mu'tazila* and *Kalam* scholars who argued that the final abode is purely a place of reward or punishment without further testing. By situating this trial in the intermediate realm (*Barzakh*) or just prior to final entry, the hadith clarifies that these five groups—children, those between Prophets, the intellectually immature, the simple-minded, and the deaf/mute—are held accountable for their specific state of being. This reinforces the Shia view that divine justice accommodates varying degrees of human capacity even in the eschatological context.
